title: Add the llm summarize command and configured request assets
objective: Add one bounded llm summarize command that accepts exactly one source mode (--path or --content), resolves the configured requestsDirectory through nodejs-common, uses the summarize prompt and output-schema assets, sends the constructed request with its files to the existing LLM completion boundary, and prints the summary using the common raw/full output formats.

branch.name: wi-0012-llm-summarize-command
branch.rationale: The work item records a bounded command and request-asset change without creating or switching a branch during intake.

request.text:
Prepare a new .docs/work-items/* to perform only the following updates:

1. add llm summarize command accepting one of the following [ --path  ] or [ --content ].
2. add requests/llm-summarize/ directory
3. add llm-summarize.outputSchema.json output schema for the llm request configuration
4. add llm-summarize.prompt.md instructing the agent to summarize <files> content
5. construct the llm request by adding <files>. if --content is provided, include a file called 'content' and include the --content text as the content of the file, inclde a note/purpose/attribute indicating it is not a file and that it is content provided by the command line
6. pull requests directory from nodejs-common configuration resolution
7. if no configuration is found error, instructing user to config ~/.llm/config.json:requestsDirectory to point to the llm repository's request directory
8. issue the llm call, and provide the summary result to the terminal, respecting common command line options --format={raw|full}

Ensure we don't build outside the above stated requirements w/out human operator approval.

scope.name: summarize-command
scope.description: Add llm summarize with one required and mutually exclusive source option: --path <path> or --content <text>.
scope.reason: Users need a dedicated command for summarizing supplied file content or command-line content without changing the existing prompt, chat, or request-file command modes.

scope.name: summarize-request-assets
scope.description: Add requests/summarize/ with summarize.prompt.md and summarize.outputSchema.json, and use those assets for the constructed LLM request.
scope.reason: The summarize operation needs a repository-owned prompt and output contract that can be resolved from the configured requests directory.

scope.name: file-input-construction
scope.description: Construct the request with its <files> collection; for --content, add a file named content containing the exact command-line text and metadata stating that it is command-line-provided content rather than a filesystem file.
scope.reason: The agent must receive all summarization material through the request file boundary while preserving the distinction between path-backed files and inline command-line content.

scope.name: requests-directory-resolution
scope.description: Resolve requestsDirectory using the nodejs-common configuration resolution convention and locate the summarize request assets below that directory.
scope.reason: Request assets must be relocatable and must use the shared application/home/environment configuration precedence rather than a hard-coded checkout path.

scope.name: completion-and-terminal-output
scope.description: Issue the existing LLM call for the constructed summarize request and print the summary result using the common --format={raw|full} behavior.
scope.reason: The command is useful only when it executes the existing completion boundary and exposes the result consistently with other CLI modes.

nonGoals.name: unrelated-cli-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not add commands, aliases, source modes, flags, interactive input, REPL behavior, or path traversal semantics beyond llm summarize with --path or --content.
nonGoals.reason: The requested feature has exactly two source options and must remain bounded until a human operator approves additional CLI behavior.

nonGoals.name: existing-command-refactor
nonGoals.description: Do not refactor or change the behavior of existing request-file, prompt, chat, continuation, help, version, debug, or output commands except for the minimal shared integration required by this command.
nonGoals.reason: The summarize command is additive and unrelated command changes would exceed the stated requirements.

nonGoals.name: request-contract-or-provider-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not redesign the existing LLM request/response schemas, provider interfaces, completion semantics, retry policy, output envelope, or provider set.
nonGoals.reason: The command must adapt the existing completion boundary rather than broaden the library contract.

nonGoals.name: configuration-convention-change
nonGoals.description: Do not invent a second configuration lookup mechanism or change nodejs-common precedence, root validation, recursive merge behavior, or provenance semantics.
nonGoals.reason: Only the existing shared configuration resolution is in scope; configuration behavior must remain standardized.

nonGoals.name: unapproved-artifacts-and-operations
nonGoals.description: Do not add request assets other than the requested directory, prompt, and output-schema files; do not change package versioning, publish, deploy, make authenticated calls during planning, or claim production/downstream integration.
nonGoals.reason: The operator explicitly limited the work to the stated updates and requires approval before scope expansion.

items.name: summarize-source-options
items.description: The CLI exposes llm summarize and accepts exactly one non-empty source option, --path <path> or --content <text>; missing, duplicate, or simultaneous source options fail with a usage/input error.
items.reason: The command must have an unambiguous source while supporting both filesystem content and command-line content.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Argument tests prove llm summarize --path <path> and llm summarize --content <text> parse as the two supported forms, while omission, duplication, simultaneous use, and empty values are rejected without an LLM call.

items.name: summarize-request-assets
items.description: The repository contains requests/summarize/summarize.prompt.md instructing the agent to summarize <files> content and requests/summarize/summarize.outputSchema.json defining the summarize response contract.
items.reason: The command must use named, repository-owned request assets rather than embedding an untracked prompt or output contract in command code.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The two requested files exist at the exact paths under requests/summarize/, the prompt explicitly directs summarization of <files> content, and the output-schema JSON parses as the schema used by the request.

items.name: files-request-construction
items.description: The constructed LLM request includes the supplied source in its <files> collection using the existing request file metadata contract; --content creates a file named content with the exact text and metadata/purpose/attribute identifying it as command-line-provided content, not a filesystem file.
items.reason: The summarize prompt consumes <files>, and inline content must not be misrepresented as a path-backed file.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Provider-boundary tests inspect the constructed request and prove path mode includes the requested path-backed file content, content mode includes name content and exact text, and content-mode metadata states that the entry is not a file and came from the command line.

items.name: configured-request-directory
items.description: The command obtains requestsDirectory through nodejs-common configuration resolution and resolves the llm-summarize assets beneath that configured directory using the shared application, home, and optional environment-root precedence.
items.reason: The request directory must follow the repository standard and must not be hard-coded to the current checkout.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Configuration tests prove the shared nodejs-common resolution is used, later configuration layers override earlier requestsDirectory values according to the common merge contract, and the selected directory is used to locate both summarize assets.

items.name: missing-configuration-guidance
items.description: When no usable configuration is found for requestsDirectory, the command fails before the LLM call with an actionable error instructing the user to configure ~/.llm/config.json:requestsDirectory to point to the llm repository request directory.
items.reason: A missing request-directory configuration cannot be recovered safely by guessing a checkout path.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A no-configuration test proves no provider/completion call occurs and the terminal error contains the exact ~/.llm/config.json:requestsDirectory guidance and explains that it must point to the llm repository request directory.

items.name: completion-and-format-output
items.description: The command issues one existing LLM completion request and prints the successful summary to the terminal with the common output behavior: raw summary text for --format=raw (the default if that is the existing common default) and the full response envelope for --format=full.
items.reason: Users need the summary in the same machine-readable or human-readable formats as the existing CLI.

acceptanceCriteria.description: CLI tests with an injected/provider-free completion prove one call is issued, raw mode emits only the summary text, full mode emits the existing full response envelope, and non-success responses use the existing error/exit behavior.

items.name: strict-scope-regression
items.description: The implementation changes only the summarize command integration, its two request assets, the required shared configuration hookup, and directly necessary tests/documentation; unrelated behavior remains unchanged.
items.reason: The operator explicitly requires approval before building outside the eight stated updates.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Changed-path review and regression tests show no unrelated command, schema, provider, package, deployment, or configuration-convention changes, and any proposed scope expansion is recorded as requiring human operator approval.
